headword_source_note: HEADWORDS ONLY, taken from the public LearnThat.org word list titled 'Verbal Advantage Word List' (retrieved 2026-09-06). The list is a study list associated with Charles Harrington Elster's 'Verbal Advantage: Ten Easy Steps to a Powerful Vocabulary'. No text from the book is reproduced here.
definitions_note: Every definition and every example sentence in this file was written for this app by automation-builder on 2026-09-06. Nothing is copied from the book.
coverage_gap: The book teaches 500 keywords across 10 levels. Only 40 headwords were retrievable from a citable public list on 2026-09-06 (learnthat.org lists 3927 and 25322 are the same 40 words; essentialenglish.review renders its per-level word pages in JavaScript and returns no words to a plain fetch). The remaining 460 headwords are NOT in this file and are NOT guessed. See the re-import hook in README.md.
reimport_hook: Drop the book in File Dump and run scripts/import_verbal_advantage.py to extract headwords only; the script then prints the words that still need our own definition and example.

cards.definition: say the same thing in your own words
cards.example: Paraphrase what she said back to her before you answer.

cards.definition: the stated reason, probably not the real one
cards.example: His ostensible reason was the invoice, the real one was the reorder.

cards.definition: wander off the point
cards.example: I digress every time I talk without a structure.

cards.definition: strange in a way that is hard to explain
cards.example: His timing on that call was uncanny.

cards.definition: open honesty even when it costs you
cards.example: I appreciated the candor more than the answer.

cards.definition: gloomy and withdrawn
cards.example: Tight money makes me morose and people feel it.

cards.definition: skilled at something through practice
cards.example: He is adept at freight, so I defer to him.

cards.definition: completely full, can absorb no more
cards.example: That category is saturated, there is no room for another me.

cards.definition: chooses what works over what is ideal
cards.example: The pragmatic move is to ship half and wait.

cards.definition: pleasant and easy to be around
cards.example: He is congenial, which is why the supplier calls go well.

cards.definition: repeat someone's exact words, or state a price
cards.example: Quote me the DDP number, not the EXW number.

cards.definition: believable on its face
cards.example: Plausible is not the same as true.

cards.definition: looks right but is actually false
cards.example: That margin math is specious, it ignores the ad spend.

cards.definition: the way in
cards.example: The ingress to the warehouse is on the north side.

cards.definition: the way out
cards.example: Every deal needs a defined egress before you sign.

cards.definition: simple and direct, no tricks
cards.example: Give me a straightforward answer on the ship date.

cards.definition: says what they think in public
cards.example: She is outspoken, which is useful and occasionally expensive.

cards.definition: says it straight without hedging
cards.example: Be forthright about the money instead of hinting at it.

cards.definition: innocently honest, no hidden angle
cards.example: His ingenuous question exposed the whole problem.

cards.definition: full of sorrow
cards.example: Do not send a dolorous follow up email, send a clear one.

cards.definition: exaggeratedly gloomy, almost comic about it
cards.example: His lugubrious update made a two day delay sound fatal.

cards.definition: gloomy and slow to warm
cards.example: He is saturnine on the phone and fine in person.

cards.definition: expects things to go well
cards.example: Optimistic forecasts are how inventory dies.

cards.definition: cheerful and friendly
cards.example: The jovial version of me closes more than the careful one.

cards.definition: calmly confident that it will work out
cards.example: I am sanguine about the quarter, not about the week.

cards.definition: silently resentful
cards.example: I went sullen instead of saying what I wanted.

cards.definition: a general dislike of people
cards.example: Burnout looks a lot like misanthropy from the outside.

cards.definition: quick and skillful with a light touch
cards.example: That was a deft way to say no.

cards.definition: clever and skillful, especially socially
cards.example: He is adroit at changing the subject.

cards.definition: skillful with the hands, or with a tricky situation
cards.example: A dexterous answer got him out of the corner.

cards.definition: good enough to do the job well
cards.example: I am proficient at PPC, I am not expert.

cards.definition: completely soaked
cards.example: I came back from the trail walk drenched.

cards.definition: soaked in something long enough to take on its character
cards.example: He is steeped in this category, twenty years of it.

cards.definition: spread through every part of something
cards.example: The doubt permeated the whole conversation.

cards.definition: filled through and through with something
cards.example: The cloth is impregnated with the coating, not sprayed.

cards.definition: fill something with a quality
cards.example: Imbue the listing with the reason it exists, not just specs.

cards.definition: heavy and soaked with liquid
cards.example: The carton was sodden when it landed.

cards.definition: completely foreign to how you normally are
cards.example: Saying no felt alien, which is exactly the problem.

cards.definition: someone who openly disagrees with the group
cards.example: Every good board needs one dissident.

cards.definition: does not fit with what is around it
cards.example: A premium price on a cheap photo is incongruous.
